symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: Nonempty finite support of the randomization law.

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Known randomization law \(p=(p_z)_{z\in Z}\), with \(Z\) defined as its support.

symbols.name: v_z
symbols.def: Known coefficient vector used by the linear effect estimator under assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: \theta
symbols.def: Fixed schedule; it is not sampled from a superpopulation.

symbols.name: \mathcal J
symbols.def: Downward-closed family of subsets observable together under some assignment.

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{\mathcal J}
symbols.def: Linear span of observable Boolean monomials.

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{\mathcal J,r}
symbols.def: Subspace generated by observable monomials of degree at most \(r\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: Generic symmetric matrix used to represent a Harshaw--Middleton--Savje design-compatible quadratic candidate.

symbols.name: g_z^{\mathrm{AS}}
symbols.def: Assignment table obtained by restricting the simplified Aronow--Samii zero-pairwise-inclusion correction to binary coordinates.

symbols.name: g_z
symbols.def: Observed-data table used when assignment \(z\) occurs.

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: Prespecified full-support objective weights; \(q\) is not a law for the fixed schedule.

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)
symbols.def: Observable functions that dominate \(f\) on the binary cube.

symbols.name: \beta_S
symbols.def: Coefficient of \(m_S\) in the unique multilinear expansion of a function on \(\Theta\).

symbols.name: \mu
symbols.def: Nonnegative weights on schedules used in the observable-margin dual.

symbols.name: \mathcal D_{\mathcal J}(q)
symbols.def: Schedule weights matching \(q\) on every observable Boolean moment.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: Generic subset used in Mobius inversion.

symbols.name: \mathbf 1_T
symbols.def: Binary schedule with ones exactly on \(T\).

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: Half-degree index in the complement-symmetry theorem.

symbols.name: x
symbols.def: Vector collecting the centered coordinates \(x_i\) in the witness.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Quadratic centered-coordinate polynomial in the witness certificates.

symbols.name: \mu^\star
symbols.def: Uniform distribution on the sixteen schedules in the all-degree dual certificate.

symbols.name: \nu^\star
symbols.def: Uniform distribution on the eight schedules in the degree-three dual certificate.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Number of independently randomized component experiments.

symbols.name: F_{\mathrm{prod}}
symbols.def: All-degree optimum for the independent product experiment.

symbols.name: F_{\mathrm{prod},r}
symbols.def: Degree \(r\) optimum for the independent product experiment.

symbols.name: X_{Bj}
symbols.def: Assignment-random block score in row \(B\), with fixed potential outcomes.

symbols.name: G_{Bj}
symbols.def: Assignment-level estimator of a conservative expected block variance bound.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: Uniform deterministic bound on block scores.

standard.name: design compatibility of the linear score

novel.justification: This proposal-specific outcome-complement symmetry has a direct design interpretation: it is satisfied when every assignment-specific score has the same total coordinate loading, including zero-sum contrast scores, because complementing all binary outcomes reflects every realized score around the same constant and leaves its randomization variance unchanged.
Uniform weighting and any paired prior weighting on binary schedules satisfy this condition; it formalizes outcome-label symmetry without restricting the fixed realized schedule.

assumptions.condition: The pairs \(\{(X_{Bj},G_{Bj}):1\le j\le B\}\) are independent across \(j\) under the row \(B\) randomization law.
\(|X_{Bj}|\le M<\infty\) for every \(B\), \(j\), and assignment atom.

standard.name: uniform boundedness implying the Lindeberg condition

definitions.name: observable-subset complex
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal J:=\{S\subseteq I:\exists z\in Z,\ S\subseteq O_z\}\).

definitions.name: Boolean observable spaces
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal J}:=\operatorname{span}\{m_S:S\in\mathcal J\}\) and \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,r}:=\operatorname{span}\{m_S:S\in\mathcal J,\ |S|\le r\}\), where \(m_S(\theta)=\prod_{i\in S}\theta_i\).

definitions.name: linear target and true randomization variance
observable-margin bound programs
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f):=\{b\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J}:b(\theta)\ge f(\theta)\ \forall\theta\in\Theta\}\), \(F_{\mathcal J}:=\min_{b\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)}\sum_\theta q_\theta b(\theta)\), and \(F_{\mathcal J,r}:=\min_{b\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,r}}\sum_\theta q_\theta b(\theta)\).

definitions.name: observable-margin dual and Pareto order
definitions.construction: Set \(\mathcal D_{\mathcal J}(q):=\{\mu\ge0:\sum_\theta\mu_\theta m_S(\theta)=\sum_\theta q_\theta m_S(\theta)\ \forall S\in\mathcal J\}\). Call \(b\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\) Pareto-admissible when no \(b'\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\) satisfies \(b'\le b\) pointwise with a strict inequality somewhere.

definitions.name: binary Aronow--Samii zero-pairwise-inclusion correction
definitions.construction: In the Horvitz--Thompson sampling-total specialization with \(\pi_{\{i\}}>0\) and \(v_{z,i}=\mathbb 1\{i\in O_z\}/\pi_{\{i\}}\), define the simplified \(a_{ik}=b_{ik}=2\) correction of Section 3.2 of \cite{AronowSamii2013} by \(g_z^{\mathrm{AS}}(\theta|_{O_z}):=\sum_{i,k\in I:\pi_{\{i,k\}}>0}\mathbb 1\{\{i,k\}\subseteq O_z\}[(\pi_{\{i,k\}}-\pi_{\{i\}}\pi_{\{k\}})\theta_i\theta_k]/[\pi_{\{i,k\}}\pi_{\{i\}}\pi_{\{k\}}]+\sum_{i\ne k:\pi_{\{i,k\}}=0}\{\mathbb 1\{i\in O_z\}\theta_i/[2\pi_{\{i\}}]+\mathbb 1\{k\in O_z\}\theta_k/[2\pi_{\{k\}}]\}\), and set \(b_{\mathrm{AS}}(\theta):=\sum_zp_zg_z^{\mathrm{AS}}(\theta|_{O_z})\).

definitions.name: independent product experiment
definitions.construction: For disjoint component schedule spaces and independent assignment laws, aggregate local scores as \(\sum_{j=1}^B a_jX_j\), use product objective weights, and retain every joint observed-data table generated by the product observation sets.

definitions.name: school-network exact-decomposition handle
definitions.construction: Starting from the published two-stage school assignment law, exposure mapping, and direct-effect score, quotient assignments and observable subsets by exact design automorphisms, introduce separator-local Boolean Mobius states, and require a rational lifting map that preserves every global domination inequality and observable margin; the solver determines whether a lossless bounded-width decomposition and a useful block exist.

statements.statement: For any finite randomization with arbitrary real probabilities on its support \(Z\), an expected rule \(b_g:\Theta\to\mathbb R\) is generated by assignment-specific observed-data tables if and only if \(b_g\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J}\). Equivalently, its unique coefficients \(\beta_S=\sum_{T\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}b_g(\mathbf 1_T)\) vanish for every \(S\notin\mathcal J\). Moreover, every \(b=\sum_{S\in\mathcal J}\beta_Sm_S\) has the assignment-level unbiased implementation \(g_z(\theta|_{O_z})=\sum_{S\subseteq O_z}(\beta_S/\pi_S)m_S(\theta)\), and \(b_g\) is universally conservative exactly when \(b_g(\theta)\ge f(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta\).
statements.justification: This identifies the complete design-estimable expected-bound space rather than a chosen algebraic subclass.
statements.gap: Proposition 1 of \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} is the degree-two pairwise case; it does not characterize arbitrary observed-data truth tables on binary schedules.
statements.consumer: It converts any finite binary exposure experiment into a complete finite set of estimability and conservativeness constraints.

statements.statement: For every full-support \(q\), the primal optimum is attained and obeys \(F_{\mathcal J}=\max_{\mu\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal J}(q)}\sum_\theta\mu_\theta f(\theta)\). A feasible \(b\) and feasible \(\mu\) are jointly optimal if and only if \(\mu_\theta>0\) implies \(b(\theta)=f(\theta)\). Every minimizer is Pareto-admissible, and every Pareto-admissible member of \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\) minimizes the displayed objective for some full-support \(q\). These conclusions hold for arbitrary real assignment probabilities on the finite support \(Z\).
statements.justification: The margin dual supplies exact certificates and the supporting-objective converse supplies the full Pareto complete class.
statements.gap: Theorem 3 of \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} characterizes admissible quadratic matrices through positive-definite matrix objectives; the proposed theorem characterizes all observable Boolean functions through full-support schedule weights and pointwise domination.
statements.consumer: A designer can enumerate all undominated expected bounds through supporting weights, without imposing rationality on the experiment.

statements.statement: If every \(p_z\), every coordinate of \(v_z\), and every \(q_\theta\) is rational, then the observable-margin primal and dual programs admit rational optimizers. Finite rational feasibility, equality of the two rational objectives, and complementary slackness form an exact primal--dual certificate; the same implementation formula yields rational assignment-level tables.
statements.justification: Rationality is needed for machine-checkable exact certificates, not for the observable-function or Pareto characterization.
statements.gap: The exact finite certificate is a computational corollary of the all-observable program, whereas \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} certifies a matrix-quadratic program.
statements.consumer: Auditors can verify a reported finite optimum using rational arithmetic with no numerical tolerance.

statements.statement: The true variance \(f\) is design-estimable if and only if \(f\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J}\). In the linear-score model this holds if and only if \(c_ic_k=0\) for every distinct pair \(i,k\) that is never jointly contained in any \(O_z\).
statements.justification: This is the exact no-slack frontier and a sanity reduction to the familiar pairwise obstruction for a quadratic target.
statements.gap: \cite{Middleton2021Unifying} and \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} give the matrix compatibility criterion over real schedules; the proposition derives its binary Boolean reduction inside the complete class.
statements.consumer: It tells experimenters when the LP is unnecessary because an unbiased variance estimator already exists.

statements.statement: Let \(H\) be symmetric and satisfy the published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje pairwise design-compatibility criterion \(H_{ik}=0\) whenever \(i\ne k\) and no \(z\in Z\) has \(\{i,k\}\subseteq O_z\). Then \(h_H\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\subseteq\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}\). If also \(H-A\succeq0\), then \(h_H\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\). The inclusion of published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje conservative quadratic candidates in the Boolean quadratic cone is strict: the constant function with value \(1+\max_{\theta\in\Theta}f(\theta)\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\) but cannot equal any \(h_H\), since every homogeneous quadratic satisfies \(h_H(0)=0\). Consequently the inclusion in the Boolean quadratic/cubic comparison cone is also strict.
statements.justification: This makes the theorem-level comparison exact: published design-compatible quadratic matrices embed into, but do not exhaust, the Boolean quadratic/cubic cone used by the witness certificate.
statements.gap: Proposition 1 and Definitions 1--2 of \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} give the pairwise matrix criterion and positive-semidefinite conservativeness; they do not state the strict binary-cube inclusion into the all-observable comparison cone.
statements.consumer: The exact \(55/36\) lower certificate can be applied to every published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje quadratic candidate without equating its smaller semidefinite program with the enlarged Boolean program.

statements.statement: Under the proposal-specific conditions \(A\mathbf 1_K=0\) and \(q_\theta=q_{\mathbf 1_K-\theta}\), \(F_{\mathcal J,2d+1}=F_{\mathcal J,2d}\) for every integer \(d\ge0\). In particular, cubic terms cannot improve the quadratic optimum, and if \(|O_z|\le3\) for every \(z\), the quadratic optimum equals the all-observable optimum. When the objective weights are not complement invariant, symmetrization need not preserve the objective and this theorem does not rule out a degree-three improvement.
statements.justification: Equal total score loadings make outcome complementation a variance-preserving design operation; paired schedule weights then identify the structural reason that the first possible gain in the witness occurs at degree four.
statements.gap: The binary inclusion-exclusion argument in \cite{Lu2019FactorialBinary} is design-specific, while the quadratic framework of \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} has no degree filtration or complement-parity theorem.
statements.consumer: It rules out fruitless odd-degree searches and gives an exact stopping rule for observation sets of size at most three.

statements.statement: For \(\mathfrak E_\star\) with uniform \(q\), \(F_{\mathcal J}=107/72\) and \(F_{\mathcal J,2}=F_{\mathcal J,3}=55/36\), so the exact gap is \(1/24\). By the strict class-inclusion proposition, every quadratic candidate allowed by the published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje framework lies in the Boolean comparison class \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}\); hence the same \(55/36\) lower certificate rules out every such published candidate, although it does not assert that \(55/36\) is the optimum of their smaller positive-semidefinite class. The displayed bounds satisfy \(r^\star(\theta)-b^\star(\theta)=[1+x_0x_1x_2x_5]/24\in\{0,1/12\}\), and \(b^\star(\theta)=3^{-1}\sum_{z=1}^3h_z^\star(\theta|_{O_z})\) with every table entry in \([0,5]\). The distribution \(\mu^\star\) certifies \(107/72\), and \(\nu^\star\) certifies \(55/36\), by exact observable-margin equalities and complementary slackness across all sixty-four schedules.
statements.justification: This exact nonnegative certificate proves that the published quadratic comparison class is globally incomplete even for a small legal binary experiment.
statements.gap: \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} optimizes only quadratic forms, and \cite{Lu2019FactorialBinary} sharpens one factorial variance without an arbitrary-design degree separation; neither contains this quartic witness or the \(1/24\) rational gap.
statements.consumer: It gives a reproducible test instance for variance-bound software and a concrete design where a higher-order rule pointwise improves a best observable quadratic rule.

statements.statement: In the binary Horvitz--Thompson sampling-total specialization, the simplified Aronow--Samii correction satisfies \(b_{\mathrm{AS}}\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\). Thus its weak conservativeness remains valid when some pairwise observation probabilities vanish, and its expected correction is one feasible point of the Boolean observable cone. Across the present model class this embedding is strict: in \(\mathfrak E_\star\), \(b^\star\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\setminus\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}\) and improves the degree-at-most-three optimum by \(1/24\).
statements.justification: This locates the canonical zero-pairwise-inclusion correction inside the proposed cone and states the strict class enlargement at theorem level.
statements.gap: Proposition 2 and Corollary 2 in Section 3 of \cite{AronowSamii2013} prove weak conservativeness of a Horvitz--Thompson correction using Young's inequality; they do not characterize every Boolean observed-data expectation, the Pareto complete class, or a strict quartic-versus-degree-at-most-three frontier.
statements.consumer: Survey samplers and exposure-design analysts can retain the published correction as a certified feasible baseline while using the observable-margin program to test and certify higher-order improvements.

statements.statement: For the independent product experiment, the full and degree-restricted optima satisfy \(F_{\mathrm{prod}}=\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2F_j\) and \(F_{\mathrm{prod},r}=\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2F_{j,r}\), even when the comparison class contains joint observed-data interactions across blocks. Primal rules add and dual certificates tensor. For \(B\) identical copies of \(\mathfrak E_\star\) with \(a_j=1/B\), the optima are \(107/(72B)\) and \(55/(36B)\), and the gap is \(1/(24B)\).
statements.justification: Tensorization shows that the finite separation survives normalization and unrestricted cross-block competitors at inferential scale.
statements.gap: The matrix framework in \cite{Middleton2021Unifying} and the optimized quadratic theory in \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} provide no product law for all-degree observable spaces or exact higher-degree gaps.
statements.consumer: Independently randomized small networks or blocks can reuse one certified lookup rule while retaining the exact advantage after aggregation.

statements.statement: The bounded-score and nondegeneracy conditions imply \(\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\bar\tau_B)/\sqrt{V_B}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\). Conditional on the denominator law \(\widehat W_B-W_B\xrightarrow{p}0\) and blockwise conservativeness \(b_{Bj}\ge\sigma_{Bj}^2\) for every \(B,j\), one has \(W_B\ge V_B\) and \(\liminf_{B\to\infty}\Pr\{\bar\tau_B\in I_B(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha\). If \(W_B\to W<\infty\), coverage converges to \(2\Phi(z_\alpha\sqrt{W/V})-1\); if \(W_B-V_B\to0\), the feasible studentized statistic converges to \(N(0,1)\).
statements.justification: Expected conservativeness alone does not imply coverage; this theorem supplies the correct \(B^{-1/2}\) standard-error scaling and the missing denominator law.
statements.gap: \cite{LiDing2017FPCLT} supplies numerator finite-population central limit theory and \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} supplies quadratic bound-estimator consistency conditions, but neither composes an all-degree observable bound with conservative studentization.
statements.consumer: It licenses asymptotic Wald inference for genuinely independent replicated binary exposure blocks using the realized higher-order lookup tables.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{school}}\) construct a nontrivial finite exposure block from the Paluck--Shepherd--Aronow school-network design whose reduced rational program is lossless for the original assignment law and direct-effect score, whose lifted primal and dual certificates verify the unreduced observable-margin optimum, and whose higher-order optimum strictly improves the best observable quadratic bound without altering the estimand?
statements.justification: This is the genuine application bottleneck: the finite theory is exact but exponential without exploitable exposure-design structure.
statements.gap: The school-data exercise in \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} is a quadratic empirical illustration based on \cite{PaluckShepherdAronow2016}, not a higher-order reanalysis, and \cite{AronowSamii2017Interference} does not supply an exact all-degree decomposition.
statements.consumer: A successful certificate would deliver the first consumer-scale comparison on the school-network substrate while preserving its actual randomization and causal contrast.

sampling_model.design: A known finite randomization \(p\) on its support \(Z\) is the only source of randomness; its support probabilities may be arbitrary positive real numbers.
sampling_model.treatment: Assignment \(z\) reveals exactly \(\theta|_{O_z}\) and the score is \(X_z=v_z^\top\theta\).
sampling_model.overlap: The set \(Z\) is the support of \(p\); a monomial is implementable only when \(\pi_S>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None in the finite characterization; the triangular-array result separately assumes a design-based law of large numbers for the chosen bound implementation.

estimand_functional: \(F_{\mathcal J}(f,q)=\min_{b\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J}:b\ge f}\mathbb E_q[b]=\max_{\mu:\mu|_{O_z}=q|_{O_z}\;\forall z}\mathbb E_\mu[f]\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Quadratic-form estimability is equivalent to pairwise design compatibility, and positive-definite targeted matrix objectives characterize the admissible quadratic bounds.
Arbitrary design--linear-estimator--variance-bound triplets are represented and estimated through quadratic matrix bounds.
Binary inclusion--exclusion yields a sharp variance improvement for a \(2^2\) factorial design.
Observed marginal distributions yield asymptotically sharp variance bounds for the difference-in-means estimator under complete randomization.
Proposition 2 and Corollary 2 give a weakly conservative Horvitz--Thompson variance correction when pairwise inclusion probabilities are zero.
Inverse-probability exposure estimators admit conservative randomization variance estimators and local-dependence asymptotics.
Finite-population central limit theorems justify randomization-based causal-effect inference for several structured designs.
Imputation and contrast constructions give conservative variance estimators for broad randomized designs and recover Neyman's estimator in standard cases.
Under random binary potential outcomes and balanced designs, CMH- and Robins-type estimators are conservative and can be asymptotically tight.

tldr: A six-coordinate three-atom experiment has an exactly certified nonnegative quartic variance-bound optimum \(107/72\), whereas every observable quadratic or cubic bound, including every published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje quadratic candidate, is at least \(55/36\); the exact separation is \(1/24\). For fixed binary potential outcomes under any finite known randomization with arbitrary real probabilities on its support, expected observed-data rules are exactly the Boolean Mobius span generated by jointly observable coordinate subsets, universal conservativeness is finite pointwise domination, and an observable-margin dual characterizes the full Pareto-admissible class. Proposal-specific complement symmetry explains the quartic threshold, independent replication preserves the block gap, and conservative studentized inference is conditional on blockwise conservativeness and a denominator law of large numbers.

project_justification.gap: The closest arbitrary-design theory, \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026}, explicitly restricts the candidate bounds to quadratic forms. The zero-pairwise-inclusion correction of \cite{AronowSamii2013} supplies a conservative Horvitz--Thompson rule but not the full observable-function cone or its Pareto frontier; the binary sharp-bound papers \cite{Lu2019FactorialBinary} and \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} treat special designs and different observable information.
project_justification.niche: Binary support makes every expected observed-data rule a finite multilinear function, so assignment-specific higher-order observability can be characterized without stochastic outcome assumptions.
project_justification.fill: The project leads with the exact \(107/72\) versus \(55/36\) quartic separation, then gives the if-and-only-if Boolean support theorem, pointwise conservative cone, observable-margin dual, Pareto complete class for real support probabilities, rational certificate corollary, product law, nonnegative implementation, and a bounded independent-block studentization theorem.

related_work: \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026}, especially Proposition 1, Theorems 1 and 3, Definitions 1--2, and Section 8, supplies the quadratic characterization and supporting-objective techniques and explicitly leaves larger bound classes open. The pairwise design-compatibility criterion implies that every published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje quadratic candidate belongs to the Boolean quadratic and cubic comparison cone used by the exact lower certificate; this inclusion is strict because the Boolean cone permits intercepts and requires domination only on \(\Theta\), whereas their class uses homogeneous forms and positive-semidefinite domination on \(\mathbb R^K\). Their use of \cite{PaluckShepherdAronow2016} is a quadratic school-data empirical illustration, not a reanalysis of the original causal conclusions. \cite{Middleton2021Unifying}, \emph{Unifying Design-based Inference: On Bounding and Estimating the Variance of any Linear Estimator in any Experimental Design}, supplies the arbitrary design--estimator--bound triplet but remains matrix-quadratic. Proposition 2 and Corollary 2 in Section 3 of \cite{AronowSamii2013} use Young's inequality to construct a weakly conservative Horvitz--Thompson correction when pairwise inclusion probabilities vanish; its binary restriction lies in \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\), but that paper does not characterize the full Boolean observable-margin cone, its Pareto complete class, or the strict quartic-versus-degree-at-most-three separation. \cite{Lu2019FactorialBinary} supplies a sharp binary inclusion--exclusion correction for the \(2^2\) factorial design, while \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} supplies sharp marginal variance bounds for difference-in-means under complete randomization. \cite{ChattopadhyayImbens2025} develops imputation and contrast variance estimators, including nonquadratic procedures, but does not characterize the complete observable-function space or its Pareto frontier. \cite{AronowSamii2017Interference} fixes the design--exposure--estimand semantics and supplies inverse-probability variance estimation and local-dependence asymptotics for the school-network consumer. \cite{LiDing2017FPCLT} supplies the finite-population limit-theory benchmark; the supporting inference result derives the numerator limit from bounded independent blocks and is explicitly conditional on blockwise conservativeness and the higher-order denominator law. \cite{AzrielKriegerKapelner2026}, \emph{Optimal Designs with Robust Inference for Binary Treatment Effects}, studies balanced designs and conservative CMH- and Robins-type inference under random binary potential outcomes, not unrestricted fixed binary schedules under a fixed arbitrary design.
technical_internal_limitation: Exact enumeration uses \(2^K\) domination inequalities, \(|\mathcal J|\) coefficients, and assignment truth tables of total size \(\sum_z2^{|O_z|}\). Independent product designs tensorize exactly, but this gives no lossless decomposition for a large connected school network. Nonnegative expected bounds also need not admit nonnegative assignmentwise tables, although the displayed quartic witness does. If \(q\) is not complement invariant, averaging a bound with its complemented version can change the objective; the odd-degree collapse then supplies no degree-three limitation, and no unsymmetric cubic-equals-quadratic claim is made.
honest_scope: All finite characterization, separation, and tensorization claims remain to be proved independently in the downstream derivation stage. The open school-network decomposition is exposed as \(\mathrm{oeq:school-exposure-block}\). The complete observable-function and Pareto results cover fixed binary schedules and ordinary finite randomized designs with arbitrary real probabilities on their support; rationality is imposed only by the exact primal--dual and assignment-table certificate proposition and by the displayed rational witness. The binary Aronow--Samii specialization records a published conservative Horvitz--Thompson baseline inside the quadratic cone and is not claimed as a new correction. There is no finite-sample coverage claim, no universal interval-shortening claim, no efficient general large-design algorithm, and no extension to real outcomes. Under full joint observability the theory reduces to exact variance estimability; under the proposal-specific complement-symmetry conditions and observed sets of size at most three it reduces to quadratic optimality, whereas no odd-degree collapse is claimed for unsymmetric objective weights. The Harshaw--Middleton--Savje school-data analysis is described only as a quadratic empirical illustration, not as a reanalysis of the original causal conclusions.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace pairwise quadratic compatibility by unique multilinear interpolation over the entire binary cube, then replace Loewner domination by pointwise domination.

seed_details.rebuttal: Their feasible objects are explicitly positive-semidefinite quadratic forms on real schedules; the exact witness separates even the larger class of all observable binary quadratics from a nonnegative quartic rule.

literature_map: The central thread is \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026}: Proposition 1 identifies estimable quadratic forms by pairwise observability, Theorems 1 and 3 characterize admissible quadratic bounds by monotone and positive-definite matrix objectives, and Section 8 asks whether larger bound classes yield improvements. \cite{Middleton2021Unifying}, under its verified title \emph{Unifying Design-based Inference: On Bounding and Estimating the Variance of any Linear Estimator in any Experimental Design}, is the matrix precursor for arbitrary design--linear-estimator--quadratic-bound triplets. The zero-observability precursor is \cite{AronowSamii2013}: Section 2 decomposes the bias caused by zero pairwise inclusion probabilities, Proposition 2 gives a Young-inequality correction, and Corollary 2 sets the conjugate exponents to two; the binary restriction is an observable quadratic baseline rather than a complete-class theorem. The binary sharp-bound thread is \cite{Lu2019FactorialBinary}, whose Theorem 1 and equation (10) sharpen the \(2^2\) factorial variance by inclusion--exclusion, and \cite{AronowGreenLee2014}, whose complete-randomization result gives consistent sharp variance-bound estimators for difference-in-means from observed marginals. \cite{ChattopadhyayImbens2025} supplies the imputation and contrast constructions in arXiv:2409.12498v2, including nonnegative conservative procedures, but no all-rule observable-space or Pareto theorem. The interference thread is \cite{AronowSamii2017Interference}, which separates design, exposure mapping, and estimand and establishes inverse-probability variance estimation with local-dependence asymptotics. The inference benchmark is \cite{LiDing2017FPCLT}, whose finite-population central limit theorems support randomization-based limits; the present supporting theorem instead uses bounded independent blocks and remains conditional on the denominator law. The school substrate is \cite{PaluckShepherdAronow2016}; the Harshaw--Middleton--Savje use of those data is a quadratic empirical illustration rather than a reanalysis of the original causal conclusions. \cite{AzrielKriegerKapelner2026}, under the verified title \emph{Optimal Designs with Robust Inference for Binary Treatment Effects}, studies balanced designs with random binary potential outcomes and conservative CMH- and Robins-type inference. These verified scopes leave the all-degree fixed-schedule cone, its Pareto class, and the exact quartic separation uncovered.
novelty_justification: The closest published result is the quadratic complete class of \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026}. The strict delta is not a relabeling: the published pairwise-compatible semidefinite class is a strict subset of the Boolean quadratic/cubic comparison cone, the proposed feasible space contains every assignment-specific observed-data truth table on the binary cube, its order is finite pointwise domination rather than Loewner domination on \(\mathbb R^K\), and an exact nonnegative quartic rule achieves \(107/72\) while the larger class of all observable binary quadratics and cubics is bounded below by \(55/36\). The zero-pairwise-inclusion correction of \cite{AronowSamii2013} embeds as an observable quadratic feasible baseline in its binary Horvitz--Thompson specialization, but it neither exhausts the cone nor supplies its Pareto frontier. Lu's binary factorial identity and Aronow--Green--Lee's marginal coupling do not cover arbitrary observation hypergraphs, a Pareto complete class, or this degree obstruction. Rational primal--dual certificates, complement parity, tensorization against cross-block competitors, and correctly scaled studentization turn the isolated finite gap into a coherent field-level result while leaving the consumer-scale school decomposition honestly open.
message: Added and formally located the Aronow--Samii zero-pairwise-inclusion correction, completed the adjacent-literature title and scope audit, preserved all prior repairs, and verified the exact rational certificates.
